item.title: Latest news on Lindsay Clancy trial as closing arguments near
item.description: Closing arguments in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial are set to begin after weeks of testimony in Massachusetts. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: World awaits Iran's response to Trump's "economic D-Day" sanctions
item.description: The Trump administration is expected to announce new sanctions against Iran meant to add economic pressure and bring Tehran back to the negotiating table. CBS News' Courtney Kealy has more.

item.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy trial continues with psychiatrist on stand
item.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial​ resumes with a psychiatrist expected back on the stand as testimony winds down in the Massachusetts murder case.

item.title: Trump escalates trade tensions with Canada
item.description: The U.S. and Canada failed to reach a trade agreement and are now in the midst of a retaliatory tariffs battle. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports, and Nelson Wiseman, a professor emeritus at the University of Toronto, joins with more insight.

item.title: U.S. set to unveil "economic D-Day" sanctions against Iran
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said new sanctions being imposed on Iran would amount to the "greatest financial offensive" ever.

item.title: Moke weakens to tropical depression as Hawaii braces for rain
item.description: Hawaii is still cleaning up from Hurricane Lala, which dumped massive amounts of rain on the islands.

item.title: Ex-NBA center ejected from WNBA game after being confronted by player
item.description: The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women should be allowed to participate in the league.

item.title: Out-of-control Hawk Fire in Reno, Nevada keeping tens of thousands evacuated
item.description: Shifting winds challenged firefighters battling the out-of-control Hawk Fire in Reno, Nevada, that was keeping tens of thousands of people evacuated.

item.title: 4 arrested after world champion boxer shot dead in South Africa
item.description: Zolani Tete made history in 2017 when he took just 11 seconds to knock out his opponent with his first punch to retain his WBO bantamweight crown.

item.description: Since then, more than 200 people have been killed in U.S. strikes in the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea.

item.title: Suspect in murders of 5 found dead day after their bodies were discovered
item.description: A quintuple murder suspect was found dead inside a vehicle in Enumclaw, Washington, a day after the bodies of five people were discovered outside Portland, Oregon, authorities said.

item.title: Sean Grayson, convicted in killing of Sonya Massey, dies in prison, attorney says
item.description: Grayson, 32, was found guilty last October of second-degree murder for the shooting of Sonya Massey and was serving a 20-year sentence.

item.title: 2 Phoenix police officers fired, arrested after violent traffic stop
item.description: Two Phoenix police officers were fired and arrested after an unreported traffic stop in which they assaulted a man and woman and shocked them with a Taser, the city's police chief said.

item.title: Trump puts autistic kids in the spotlight and cuts agencies built to protect them
item.description: Researchers and disability rights advocates warn that the dismantling of the Education Department and its erosions of civil rights oversight risk widening the disparities autistic children face.

item.title: How some are keeping manual driving alive
item.description: For generations of drivers, getting behind the wheel meant you had to be able to use a stick shift. Now, new data shows that manual-transmission cars have all but disappeared. But some are keeping the driving skill alive. CBS News' Bradley Blackburn goes on a ride.

item.title: Navy sailor on USS Lincoln says dad was arrested by immigration officials
item.description: Historically rare, immigration arrests of military spouses and parents have become more common under the second Trump administration.

item.title: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections, cites "huge risk"
item.description: After Ukraine's fired defense minister publicly called for wartime elections, Zelenskyy said it would risk splitting the country.

item.title: Iran's president defends U.S. memorandum of understanding as best path forward
item.description: The new head of Iran's supreme national security council issued the warning to countries who join the U.S.'s economic war on Tehran.

item.title: Fast-growing Hawk Fire near Reno, Nevada forces thousands to evacuate
item.description: The fire apparently began Saturday and grew significantly throughout the day, fueled by strong, gusty winds, low humidity and dry vegetation.

item.title: Jared Kushner and Hakeem Jeffries met as midterm elections loom
item.description: The meeting came with Democrats expected to take control of the House in the November elections, which would put Jeffries in line to become the next House speaker.

item.title: 8/23/2026: Ghost Train; One Mother's Story; Wild Concerto
item.description: First, the state of high-speed rail in the U.S. Then, Rachel Goldberg-Polin: The 60 Minutes Interview. And, turning recordings of animals into music.

item.title: Bunny Levine, "Gilmore Girls" and "La La Land" actress, dies at 97
item.description: Bunny Levine worked as a school librarian for 25 years before pursuing her passion for acting and performing.

item.title: Dr. Oz says MMR is "not a lethal vaccine" despite Trump's comments
item.description: Dr. Mehmet Oz, the administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, said the MMR vaccine is "not a lethal vaccine," despite President Trump's claims in recent days.

item.title: Kashkari: Inflation could be extended as Canada fight goes on
item.description: Neel Kashkari, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, said the tariff fight with Canada could extend U.S. inflation, should the tense trade dynamic between the historically allied countries continue.

item.title: 8/23: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Minneapolis Fed President and CEO Neel Kashkari joins to discuss the U.S. debt hitting a record $40 trillion amid persistent inflation and market uncertainty. Plus, Rep. Byron Donalds joins fresh off his primary victory, and Massachusetts Democrat Rep. Seth Moulton discusses his primary challenge to a longtime incumbent.

item.title: Mexican official accused by U.S. of drug trafficking abruptly resigns again
item.description: Sinaloa Gov. Ruben Rocha Moya is accused of allegedly colluding with the infamous Sinaloa Cartel to distribute drugs inside the U.S.

item.title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll considering stepping down, sources say
item.description: U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is considering stepping down from his post by the end of the year, two people familiar with the matter told CBS News Saturday.

item.title: Pilot reports possible burn injuries after passenger's laptop catches fire
item.description: "I think we have about four to five passengers that were burned by the laptop," a pilot can be heard saying in air traffic control audio obtained by CBS News.
